title: She was doing everything right.
paragraphs: Because you can be faithful in activity and still be far in intimacy.
You won’t see it at first.
Even what God seems to require.
And yet… there’s a dryness you can’t explain.
A tension in your chest you can’t pray away.
A quiet question you’re afraid to say out loud:
“Why do I feel so far from God… while doing things for Him?”
This is the warning hiding in Martha’s story.
“But Martha was distracted with much serving…”
And that’s where shame begins to creep in.
Because you don’t feel like a sinner.
Not because you don’t love it…
…but your soul hasn’t felt Him in a while.
And then comes the subtle shift.
And slowly, without noticing, your heart starts to harden.
That line didn’t come from nowhere.
That came from a heart stretched too thin…
and slowly losing sight of who Jesus really is.
When service turns into silent resentment.
When obedience turns into emotional distance.
And here’s the truth most people don’t say:
You can be deeply involved in ministry…
Because the issue was never the serving.
It was the priority of the soul.
“Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things…”
And then He points to Mary.
She sat at the feet of Jesus.
When was the last time you sat with Jesus…
but just to be with Him?
It’s about sin at the level of the heart.
The belief that your activity can sustain your identity.
The assumption that your usefulness secures your worth.
The subtle lie that you are “doing enough” for God…
Some scholars interpret Martha’s distraction not merely as busyness, but as misordered love—where even good actions become idols when they replace devotion.
This is where the Gospel enters.
You were never saved by your service.
You were never loved because of your performance.
You were never accepted because of your consistency.
You are saved by Jesus Christ alone.
Jesus lived the life you couldn’t.
And then He went to the cross.
For all the moments you chose many things…
And when He said, “It is finished,”
So you don’t just get forgiven.
This is not a call to try harder.
This is a call to come back.
He still calls like that today.
You don’t need to prove anything.
You don’t need to earn your place.
You don’t need to fix yourself first.
Lay down the need to be “enough.”
What has been louder than Jesus in my life?
What “good things” have taken His place?
Where have I been serving… but not surrendering?
Because the good portion is still available.
And it will not be taken from you.
If this stirred something in you…
